basics.name: IFToMM terminology for mechanism and machine science (IFToMM Dictionary / 'Terminology for the Mechanism and Machine Science', by the IFToMM Permanent Commission for the Standardization of Terminology, formerly Commission A)
basics.url: https://iftomm-terminology.antonkb.nl/ (the 'IFToMM dictionaries online', Version 3.1, May 2014; the English dictionary is at https://iftomm-terminology.antonkb.nl/2057/frames.html). Linked from the commission's page https://iftomm-world.org/commissions/permanent-commission-for-the-standardization-of-terminology/
basics.resource_type: classification system (a standard terminology: a numbered, subject-ordered dictionary of terms with definitions in four languages, published in print and as an online dictionary)
basics.cost: Free online. The printed editions in the journal Mechanism and Machine Theory (Elsevier) are paywalled (e.g. the 2003 edition is marked closed access in OpenAlex; ScienceDirect articles are sold individually)
basics.license: No licence or copyright notice was found on the online dictionary pages, so by default all rights are reserved by IFToMM [uncertain]. The printed journal editions are copyright Elsevier. What this means for the encyclopedia: using the proper term names is fine (names are facts), and linking to the dictionary is fine, but quote definitions only briefly with a citation and don't copy the dictionary wholesale
basics.language: Four official IFToMM languages: English, French, German and Russian. The site has monolingual dictionaries and bilingual side-by-side views for every pair (12 pairs). Coverage differs: chapter 14 (Transportation) is in English and Russian only, and chapter 16 (Compliant Mechanisms) is in English only. National translations have been made in Japan, China, Romania, the Czech Republic and Poland (Segla 2014), but they are not on the site
basics.year: The commission was founded in 1969. Printed editions in Mechanism and Machine Theory: 1983 (vol. 18 no. 6, English master version), 1991 (vol. 26 no. 5, four languages, 763 terms), 1997 (vol. 32 no. 6, abbreviations/symbols and graphical symbols for mechanisms), and 2003 (vol. 38 nos. 7-10, 3rd edition, special issue edited by T. Ionescu). The online dictionary started about 2004; its latest version is 3.1 (May 2014). In 2019 a new online editor (THEDI) inside DMG-Lib was introduced for future releases
basics.access_barrier: none for the online dictionary (no login). Academic licence or paywall for the printed journal versions
basics.image_license: Not applicable: the dictionary has no figures, animations or videos (only flag and fold/unfold icons were found in the chapter pages)
basics.authority_level: official standard (international scientific federation). IFToMM is the international federation for mechanism and machine science; its terminology commission of nearly 60 specialists from 25 countries (to 2014) wrote the definitions under agreed rules for defining terms, and the printed editions appeared in IFToMM's own journal

coverage.covers: The whole vocabulary of mechanism and machine science, not only mechanism types: structure of machines and mechanisms (components such as crank, rocker, cam, pawl, latch, ratchet, stop; sub-assemblies such as kinematic pairs, couplings and clutches; mechanism types such as step, Geneva, differential and self-locking mechanisms), kinematics, dynamics, machine control and measurement, robotics, general terms, rotor dynamics, vibrations and non-linear oscillations, stability, biomechanics, gearing, mechatronics, transportation machinery and logistics, and compliant mechanisms. The English online dictionary has about 1,795 term entries across 16 chapters (my count of headwords: e.g. chapter 1 Structure 125, chapter 3 Dynamics 352, chapter 12 Gearing 226, chapter 16 Compliant Mechanisms 30). The 2003 printed edition had a core of 771 terms in four languages plus a supplement of 823 English terms
coverage.organisation: Classified (systematic) order: numbered chapters and sub-chapters by subject (e.g. 1 Structure > 1.1 Components > 1.1.49 PAWL), with an alphabetical index and a free-text search box. Each term links to the terms used in its definition. For someone who doesn't know the terms this works poorly: you must already know a word to search for it, the chapters are arranged by academic discipline rather than by what you want to do, and there are no pictures
coverage.scope_match: medium. It is the authority for the proper names of mechanism types and elements (pawl, latch, ratchet, self-locking mechanism, step mechanism, Geneva mechanism, differential, harmonic drive, living hinge, bistable compliant mechanism), which the encyclopedia needs for its 'engineering term in brackets'. But most of its roughly 1,800 terms are theory (kinematics, dynamics, vibration, control), not connection types, and it gives no pictures, uses or design advice
coverage.taxonomy_used: Subject chapters, 16 top-level groups in the online version: 0 General; 1 Structure of Machines and Mechanisms (1.1 Components, 1.2 Sub-assemblies, 1.3 Mechanisms); 2 Kinematics; 3 Dynamics; 4 Machine Controls and Measurement; 5 Robotics; 6 General Terms; 7 Dynamics, Supplement; 8 Rotor Dynamics and Measurement; 9 Vibrations and Non-linear Oscillations; 10 Stability; 11 Biomechanics; 12 Gearing (12.1-12.6, including 12.6 Geared Mechanisms); 13 Mechatronics; 14 Transportation Machinery and Logistics; 16 Compliant Mechanisms (listed as 15 in Segla 2014). Within 'Structure', mechanisms are named by kinematic structure (kinematic pairs: lower/higher, revolute, prismatic, helical, cylindrical, spherical, planar; closure: force-closed vs form-closed) and by function (guidance, function-generating, path-generating, step, dwell, differential, self-locking, adjustable), following the Reuleaux / German VDI tradition
coverage.example_types: Pawl [click, detent]; latch; ratchet; stop; self-locking mechanism; step mechanism; pilgrim-step mechanism; dwell mechanism; Geneva mechanism [Geneva drive]; geared Geneva mechanism; differential mechanism; adjustable mechanism; universal [Cardan, Hooke's] joint; clutch; coupling; Scotch-yoke mechanism; wedge mechanism; screw mechanism; epicyclic [planetary] gear train; wave gear train [harmonic drive]; enveloping [hourglass, globoidal] worm; spiroid gear; contrate [face] gear; lantern gear [cage gear]; force-closed and form-closed kinematic pairs; bistable compliant mechanism; living hinge; cross-axis flexural pivot; cartwheel hinge; notch flexure hinge
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering and mechanism/machine science (research and teaching). Nothing specific to 3D printing, CNC, woodwork or hobby making
coverage.item_count: About 1,795 English term entries online (headwords counted across the 16 chapter pages, September 2026); German about 1,614, French about 1,600, Russian about 1,766 (chapters 14 and 16 missing in some languages). Printed 2003 edition: 771 core terms in four languages plus 823 English supplement terms (1,594). 1991 edition: 763 terms
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: no (only generic 'clutch' and 'coupling'); self-locking: yes, 'self-locking mechanism' is defined (cannot transmit motion and power from output back to input); hand-release only: no; one-way/ratchet: yes, 'pawl [click, detent]' (prevents motion in one direction) and 'ratchet'; indexing/detent: yes, 'step mechanism' (one-way output with periodic dwells), 'Geneva mechanism', 'dwell mechanism' and 'detent' as a synonym of pawl; over-centre: only indirectly ('dead point', 'limit position of a mechanism'), no toggle entry; compliant: yes, a whole chapter (30 terms: compliant joint, flexure hinge, living hinge, bistable and monolithic compliant mechanisms, pseudo-rigid-body model); print-in-place: no; gear trains/gearboxes: yes, strongly (226 gearing terms, including epicyclic, differential and harmonic-drive gear trains); powered connectors: only 'actuator', 'intelligent actuator' and 'compliant actuator', no electromagnets or solenoid latches; adhesive types: no
coverage.entry_structure: Number (e.g. 1.1.49), term in capitals with synonyms in square brackets (e.g. 'PAWL [CLICK, DETENT]', 'UNIVERSAL [CARDAN, HOOKE'S] JOINT'), and a one-sentence definition with hyperlinks to other defined terms. An 'unfold' button shows the definitions of the linked terms inline. Bilingual views put the entry in two languages side by side under the same number. No figures, examples of use, degrees of freedom tables, design rules or CAD
coverage.audience_level: research / professional / undergraduate (mechanism and machine science specialists, lecturers and translators)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: low. Definitions are short and exact but written in the field's own jargon (e.g. 'link', 'kinematic pair', 'frame'), there are no pictures, and you can only find a term if you already know its name. Its value to beginners is indirect: it gives the proper name and aliases to put in brackets
usefulness.has_images: no (text-only definitions; the printed 1997 edition has graphical symbols for representing mechanisms, but these are not on the online dictionary) [uncertain]
usefulness.gaps: No pictures, examples or 'what is it used for'; no plain-English or beginner names (many everyday names such as 'toggle clamp', 'freewheel', 'snap fit', 'detent ball', 'quick-release' are missing); nothing on fasteners, adhesives, powered latches, torque limiters or hand-release locks; no route from a need to a term (index and search only); French and German lack the two newest chapters; the online version has not been updated since 2014 and some links on the site are broken
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: medium. Each term has a stable anchor on its chapter page, so an entry can link to its official definition, e.g. https://iftomm-terminology.antonkb.nl/2057/01.html#1.1.49 (PAWL [CLICK, DETENT]) or the English-German view https://iftomm-terminology.antonkb.nl/2057_1031/01.html#1.1.49. But the site is frame-based and hosted on a private-looking domain after moving from TU Delft, so the links may not be long-lived [uncertain]
usefulness.reusable_data: scrape-only: static HTML chapter pages per language (and language pair), consistently structured (number, bold term with bracketed synonyms, definition), so a term list with translations could be extracted. No API or download. No licence is stated, so reusing the definitions needs permission; reusing term names and numbers as references is low-risk [uncertain]
usefulness.maintained: Online and working (checked September 2026), but frozen at Version 3.1 (May 2014); the commission-members page is dated April 2010, and the 'Return to Start Page of the website' link is broken (404). The earlier TU Delft address (www.iftomm.3me.tudelft.nl, cited in Segla 2014) returned no snapshot from the Wayback Machine availability API (a fuller check was rate-limited) [uncertain]. The commission itself is still active (2026 page lists chair Prof. Jun Zhang, Fuzhou University), and new work moved to the THEDI editor inside DMG-Lib (2019), whose multilingual thesaurus had 1,784 concepts in September 2026
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Headword plus synonyms in brackets ('PAWL [CLICK, DETENT]'), which is exactly the project's 'plain term (engineering term)' pattern in reverse, so aliases should be a field. (2) Stable hierarchical IDs (1.1.49) that survive reordering. (3) Side-by-side language view for translations. (4) Inline 'unfold' of the terms used inside a definition, a handy way to explain jargon without leaving the page. (5) The commission's rules for writing definitions (Segla 2014): no circular definitions, no negative definitions, simplest possible language, don't invent terms just to pair with others, and 'when in doubt, leave it out'. (6) Separating structure (components, sub-assemblies, mechanisms) from function (guidance, step, dwell, self-locking, adjustable) as two classification axes
usefulness.design_rules_given: No. It is a vocabulary; it defines quantities (backlash, pressure angle, module, contact ratio) but gives no numbers for design
usefulness.file_formats: HTML web pages (frame-based, one page per chapter per language or language pair). The underlying work was compiled from Word files via XML into compiled HTML help (CHM-style) files, per Segla 2014. Printed/PDF journal articles from Elsevier
usefulness.terminology_value: high, the top authority for this field: official definitions and standard names for mechanism and machine science terms, with synonyms and equivalents in English, French, German and Russian. Best source for the bracketed engineering term and its translations in those four languages; weaker for everyday maker names and for other languages
usefulness.decision_support: None: no selector, flow chart, filters or comparison tables. Only a search box, an alphabetical index and a subject table of contents
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Builds on earlier national terminologies such as Levitskii et al.'s Russian 'Teoriya mekhanizmov: Terminologiya' (1964) and the German VDI guideline 2127 on mechanism terms (as cited in Ionescu, Bogelsack and Leinonen 2004). It feeds and overlaps the DMG-Lib multilingual thesaurus (the IFToMM commission page links to DMG-Lib, and the THEDI editor for the dictionary is part of DMG-Lib). Cite the IFToMM dictionary or the 2003 Mechanism and Machine Theory edition for definitions rather than DMG-Lib
